planes.name: Platform
planes.purpose: The inherited base: one base resource, identity, grants, audit, erasure, tenancy — everything arrives by inheritance, nothing by discipline.

planes.name: Canonical record
planes.purpose: The operational data spine: ingestion edges, the strangler'd legacy estate, the CDM-derived store, the business-event ledger, master data.

planes.name: Evidence & judgment
planes.purpose: Recorded observations over any subject: questions, judgment ledger, banding, evidence adjudication, lineage, licences.

planes.name: Deterministic authority
planes.purpose: Rules, DMN decision tables, compliance projection, constraint planning — declarations that decide, with audit trails.

planes.name: Orchestration
planes.purpose: BPMN processes, event-triggered dispatch, execution identity and the governed-invocation machinery service tasks run through.

planes.name: Agents & models
planes.purpose: The agent runtime, model residency zones, assistant surfaces, quality gating and releases — agents as users, never a parallel path.

planes.name: Surfaces
planes.purpose: Everything rendered from the declarations: A2UI surfaces, admin, canvas, showcase, localization, telemetry.

contexts.name: Platform
contexts.mission: The base resource and its inherited concerns; the cross-substrate battery proving the seams.

terms.definition: Every resource uses AshEnterprise.Platform.Resource; opting out is explicit and greppable, never silent.
Everything a policy check needs is precomputed once per request into ActorContext; a check that queries is a bug, not a slow path.
The cross-substrate integration battery, run over its own reference instantiation on dependency bumps.

contexts.name: Accounts
contexts.mission: Identity: users, teams, from the published schema commons.

terms.definition: A person who can sign in, and the actor every policy is evaluated against.
A tenant.
A node in the organizational hierarchy, and the unit of the Local and Deep access levels.
A group of users; by type either a principal that can own records and hold roles, or a lightweight bucket for sharing.

contexts.name: Security
contexts.mission: Authorization as data: (role, privilege, depth) grants as a pure union; the automation principal and its grants.

terms.definition: A named bag of (privilege, depth) grants.
One (resource, verb) pair that a role can grant.
The (role, privilege, depth) triple; depth scopes it to global, business unit or record.
An explicit share: (principal, record, rights).
Assigns a role to an automation principal, scoped to a business unit (ADR 0043).

contexts.name: Flags
contexts.mission: Feature flags, tenant by tenant, resolved once per request into the actor's context.

terms.definition: The keys this build declares, and the ones the deployment killed.
One tenant's decision for one key: off, on, or on for named people, teams, business-unit subtrees and a percentage.
Whether a row is on for a person, pure.

contexts.name: Audit
contexts.mission: The tamper-evident, tenant-scoped event ledger every projection reads from.

terms.definition: The central audit trail.
Each chain's rows link by hash; the verifier walks every chain and reports where, if anywhere, it stops adding up.
A read model built from the event log; how far each projector has processed is its checkpoint.

contexts.name: Erasure
contexts.mission: Crypto-shredding and retention: the right to be forgotten over an append-only ledger.

terms.definition: The unit that one key encrypts and one shred destroys.
One erasure scope's data-encryption key, stored wrapped under the master key.
Destroying a scope's key renders everything the scope covered unreadable, without rewriting a single appended row.

contexts.name: Standards
contexts.mission: The advisory standards review over this repository's own code; never fails a build.

terms.definition: The cheapest place to use a fast typed judgment is not the product; it is the tooling around it — the review judges this repository's own code.
A finding here never fails a build; it is reported for a person to weigh.
The standing review records the last checkout HEAD it judged in full, per tenant and repository.

contexts.name: Faults
contexts.mission: Named fault points: places in production code where a test can make the process fail.

terms.definition: A named place in production code where a test can make the process fail, because the code that commits is the code that must stop.
A test arms a fault point by name before the code under test runs.
The fault that kills the calling process outright, uncatchable — the nearest thing to the node dying that a test can do without stopping the node.

contexts.name: Reference
contexts.mission: Published-model reference data; do not invent your nouns.

terms.definition: Published-model reference data, generated from the vendored corpus rather than invented.
Generated by mix cdm.gen.resource from a resolved corpus document.
The frozen, hybrid, vendored corpus the reference data is generated from.

contexts.name: Ingestion
contexts.mission: External corpora land as Ash resources, not staging schemas.

terms.definition: The immutable raw-landing record for one external object.
External corpora land into an Ash resource, not a staging schema.
The deterministic fixture tap lands records as source objects.

edges.note: Lands as resources shaped by the schema commons.

contexts.name: Integration
contexts.mission: The provider edge: declared operations, webhook ingress, scoped landing under erasure scopes.

terms.definition: One of an actor's own provider accounts, mapped to the connection that holds its credentials; the unit of credential ownership is the user account.
One generic action and one code interface per provider operation, with a vendored spec pinned by sha-256 and one transport per provider.
A provider webhook delivery, recorded once.

edges.note: Scoped landing; nothing lands outside an erasure scope.

contexts.name: Legacy estate
contexts.mission: The projected read model over the strangler'd legacy schema.

terms.definition: A platform resource whose data layer is a compatibility view over a legacy table rather than a table this application owns.
A typed expression over a legacy relation's columns, with a proven inverse.
The read model over the legacy users table.

edges.note: The drain projects ledger rows into canonical actions.

contexts.name: Legacy twins
contexts.mission: Twin/shadow resources proving projection parity before cutover.

terms.definition: The legacy relation declared as an ordinary Ash resource, so a mapping can name its columns and have them mean something.
The twin and its projection must agree before anything cuts over; the twin makes the disagreement visible.
The legacy estate is projected, not cut over.

contexts.name: Change ledger
contexts.mission: The change ledger a legacy trigger writes; the drain turns a row into a canonical action in one transaction.

terms.definition: The row a legacy trigger writes recording that a legacy write happened.
An at-least-once worker that projects a ledger row into a canonical action in one transaction.
A write in the old schema; the chain legacy write → ledger row → drain → canonical action is the strangler demo in one line.

contexts.name: Canonical store
contexts.mission: The CDM-derived operational store on the temporal validity substrate.

terms.definition: A person in the operator's world: the organizer of a meeting, a message correspondent, a task's assignee.
A thread: an email thread, a chat channel or DM, or a face-to-face the operator logged.
One sent or received item in a conversation, with its sender, timestamp and direction.
A commitment with a status.
One calendar event, projected from landed source objects.

edges.note: Findings project from the event log (ADR 0035).

contexts.name: Business events
contexts.mission: The chained, commit-ordered discrete event ledger derived from canonical writes.

terms.definition: The business-event ledger, a :ledger macro instantiated on the platform base so the tables are this application's.
A partition of the ledger's chain, lock and feed; every row declares its residency tag.
What every row declares.

contexts.name: Master data
contexts.mission: Versioned mappings, deterministic entity resolution, survivorship, non-destructive merges over golden records.

terms.definition: A versioned schema mapping, ingress or egress.
One landed source row, mapped into canonical shape by the batch's pinned mapping.
One (staged record, golden record) candidate pair with its score and per-rule explanation.
The cross-reference registry: which external source identity points at which golden record, right now — temporal, one open period per identity.
The survived, merged record the operational store reads; merges are non-destructive.

contexts.name: Lineage
contexts.mission: Run-event lineage emitted from action notifications.

terms.definition: One operation: every lineage event that shared a correlation id.
One lineage job, per tenant, named structurally.
One lineage run: one job inside one operation, keyed by the event's run id.

edges.note: Observes action notifications, emits run events.

contexts.name: Exports
contexts.mission: Bulk export out: a tenant's data as CSV, under the same policies as every other read.

terms.definition: The export privilege: one more grantable (resource, verb) row, held by default by the tenant's Administrator role and nobody else.
Which resources are exportable.
The stream of one exportable resource, read in keyset pages as the requester.

contexts.name: System One
contexts.mission: Declared questions, the append-only judgment ledger, banding, admitted facts, human verdicts; evidence adjudication as assertions.

terms.definition: One append-only observation per question per call, in the judgment ledger.
A person's confirmation or correction of a recorded observation.
Which band-table row a judged answer fell into.
One calibration record per (family, question hashes, model digest, runtime version, eval-set hash, region), whose metrics earn a band-table proposal.
The materialised-facts table: what the set evaluator, the filters and the standing queries read.
The aggregate evidence verdict one packet's adjudication produced — the admission's provenance.

edges.note: Questions declared on canonical subjects; observations recorded, never authoritative.
Judgments as predicates over sets (ADR 0048, proposed).

contexts.name: Credentialing
contexts.mission: The credentialing vertical slice composing evidence, judgment and process end to end.

terms.definition: The organization a clinician works for.
A clinician a clinic is onboarding.
A clinician's licence or certification, recorded at the clinic and activated with the registry before the clinician may practise there.

contexts.name: Licences
contexts.mission: Dependency licence adjudication; judgments declared on dependency resources.

terms.definition: A third-party package at the version the lockfile resolves: the subject of the licence policy.
The declared policy the dependency's questions are answered against.
Which rung answers a licence subject; a release reaches the model only when its declaration cannot settle the questions.
The release declares exactly one licence id the policy classifies; every question is answered from the id.

contexts.name: Signatures
contexts.mission: Signature and acknowledgement requests: the five fragments on the platform base.

terms.definition: People asked to sign or acknowledge exact document versions, in order.
One document version a request shows, with its SHA-256 copied from it.
One person asked, acting on their own row.
One thing that happened, append-only.

contexts.name: Compliance
contexts.mission: Findings projected from the event log under immutable, content-hashed rule bundles; missing evidence is unknown, never compliant.

terms.definition: A compliance catalog: the stable identity a stream of immutable revisions hangs off.
The immutable, content-hashed compiled artifact: the effective rule bundle for an organization at a point in time.
The current compliance state of one subject against one control.
An approval-bearing exception: a replacement of a rule, or a waiver of one, with the accountability the framework requires.
The append-only record of one evaluation: what the engine decided and why.

contexts.name: Decisions
contexts.mission: DMN decisions as versioned resources over a native expression engine; band tables live here.

terms.definition: A published decision document, compiled into an immutable versioned snapshot.
What a decision was asked, and what it answered.
The versioned threshold table a judged answer is banded against, earned by a certified calibration run.

contexts.name: Planning
contexts.mission: Constraint models propose; declarations and people commit.

terms.definition: One immutable planning model version.
A tenant's binding of (model key, purpose) to the definitions a plan is made with.
One planning run.
One candidate plan a run proposed.
One check of one candidate.

contexts.name: Processes
contexts.mission: BPMN documents compiled to immutable graphs, executed by a token interpreter.

terms.definition: A published process document, compiled into an immutable versioned graph.
One run of a process, pinned to the definition version it started on.
One live branch of a running process.
A work item waiting on a person: an approval, a review, a decision someone has to make.
A declaration that something happening in the audit log should start a process.
How far the trigger sweep has read into one tenant's audit chain.

edges.note: Via the configured DecisionResolver; no package dependency.
Service tasks run as governed invocations (ADR 0055).

contexts.name: Process instances
contexts.mission: Host process instances and the dispatched-cursor event triggers.

terms.definition: Which definition of a given key this tenant runs.
Events trigger processes through a dispatched cursor, not a handler.
Approvals and process modelling stay inside Ash.

contexts.name: Automation
contexts.mission: What a tenant's recipes react to when the thing that happened is not an audited tenant write.

terms.definition: A fact recorded into a tenant's audit chain so that a subscription can match it: a user deactivated, a sign-in refused, a break-glass session approved, an API key issued, an inbound alert.
The alerts that share a key, from the first one that fired until it closes; a duplicate alert joins the open incident.
How inbound alerts reach occurrences.

contexts.name: Execution
contexts.mission: Identity resolution and the governed-invocation lease/job handoff every consequential act runs through.

terms.definition: One governed invocation: the invocation fragment on the platform base.
One version of an agent.
A release: an immutable set of the things that were tested together, named by digest, and the one pointer that says which set is live.
A person's act on one invocation from the recovery surface, with who did it and why; an act that is refused leaves no row.

contexts.name: Execution sources
contexts.mission: Provenance sources for executions.

terms.definition: The provenance a governed invocation names for what it read or acted on.
A target names <resource module>.<action> and must carry an effects declaration.
An action declares the effects it may have; a governed act runs only through a target that carries one.

contexts.name: Agents
contexts.mission: Governed invocations, durable runs, the coding-agent bridge; effects declared per action.

terms.definition: A persistent coding-agent session identity and lifecycle.
One requested unit of coding-agent work: a prompt handed to the process of a session, the messages it streamed back, and the tool invocations it asked for.
A coding agent's tool call, asked of the person its run belongs to.
The terminal's prompts, each answering from ordinary reads as the calling actor — the same read actions, under the same policies, the matching web surface uses.

edges.note: Same action layer and policies as every other actor (thesis 5).

contexts.name: AI
contexts.mission: Model wiring and residency: in-zone inference; leaving the zone is a disclosure.

terms.definition: One model call: the flow record.
Which model a profile runs, what it may be used for, whether it is known to answer, and what it is restricted from.
Inference runs in-zone; leaving the zone is a disclosure.

contexts.name: Residency zones
contexts.mission: The residency policy deciding which zones instruments may run in; configuration, never code.

terms.definition: A declared boundary with a jurisdiction, a classification ceiling and the residency restrictions it cannot satisfy.
May this tenant's data be answered by an instrument of this residency class?
Leaving the zone is a disclosure, not a second authorization model.

contexts.name: Assistant
contexts.mission: The host assistant and its evaluation harness.

terms.definition: One assistant conversation: the person's question-and-answer history.
One question or one answer in a thread.
A surface the person composed in the agent chat and pinned: a personal app on their launcher.

contexts.name: Legacy agent
contexts.mission: The agent console over the legacy estate.

terms.definition: The agent console over the legacy estate.
The projected read model over the strangler'd legacy schema.
Two derived UI layers that overlap, and the overlap is the point of the decision.

contexts.name: Quality
contexts.mission: Agent-quality suites and gated, attested releases.

terms.definition: A suite of evaluation cases for an agent: a key and a version, draft then published then retired.
One run of a published suite against a candidate agent: running, then finished.
What one case of a suite run scored, at one epoch; written once, never changed.

contexts.name: Agent protocol
contexts.mission: The agent-client wire adapter: sessions and permission requests over host behaviours.

terms.definition: An agent-client session; the host owns the session table and its store.
A permission the agent asks of a person, resolved through the host's approvals.
What an arriving prompt may act on, resolved by the host's session store.

contexts.name: Surfaces
contexts.mission: The agent-renderable experience layer bound to host resources.

terms.definition: A surface renders from a payload the experience library encodes; it renders declared actions and adds no authorization of its own.
The agent-renderable payload generated from the resource declarations.
A client-side catalog renders the payload.

edges.note: Renders declared actions; no parallel authorization (ADR 0033).

contexts.name: Canvas
contexts.mission: The dev-only object graph inspector.

terms.definition: The dev-only object graph over the running application's records.
The inspector that renders a record from its own declaration, with no per-type page.
The contract the dev-only object graph is described by; the library tier implements it.

contexts.name: Showcase
contexts.mission: The guided demonstration estate.

terms.definition: The governed-invocation programme's scenario as a running application a person can click through, built in slices over the demo data.
One tour segment of the showcase, added on top of the demo data.
The showcase's panel that arms named fault points, so a tour can show what a death between commits does.

contexts.name: Localization
contexts.mission: Gettext catalogs and library-shipped translations.

terms.definition: A translation catalog; the POT templates are derived from the source calls, like migrations are from the resources.
Translations a dependency ships for its own strings, extracted with their own metadata.
The application's own text: static, in source control, shipped with the app.

contexts.name: Telemetry
contexts.mission: Tracer → OpenTelemetry → OTLP wiring.

terms.definition: The instrumentation seam actions and transports report through.
The wiring that ships spans off-node to the collector.
The wire the exporter ships over: tracer to the telemetry SDK to the collector.

contexts.name: Artifacts
contexts.mission: The artifact registry: every versioned thing a person authors, reviews or releases, declared once.

terms.definition: An entry naming a resource and what the artifact pages need to know about its rows: its version, lifecycle, content hash, scope and differ.
A module that compares two versions by meaning — graph nodes, cases, tools — never by text.
The comparison of one version against its predecessor or any other version, by meaning.
Identity, version, lifecycle, content hash, provenance and who published it, with the run it was opened from.

contexts.name: Documents
contexts.mission: The documents surface: issuing real documents from the host's own data through the paper kernel (`github.com/lukegalea/ash_paper`).

terms.definition: What a document kind is rendered with (ADR 0062's binding, on the paper kernel's vocabulary): `AshPlanning.Fragment.Binding` on the platform base, in table `paper_bindings`, one temporal row per (organization, kind).
One attempt to produce a document: `AshPaper.Fragment.Run` on the platform base, in table `paper_runs`, tenant-scoped in the `AshEnterprise.Documents` domain.
A rendered document waiting for a person (R10): `AshPlanning.Fragment.Candidate` on the platform base, in table `paper_drafts`.
One wording clause a document may carry, per locale: tenant data, drafted and admitted by people, in the table `paper_clauses`.
The questions a requirement is still asking the signed-in person, one row per fact one of their blocked runs is missing (R1).
A person's answer to a question a requirement asked (R1, R8): the record of who answered what, on which blocked run, and the fact it admitted.

substrates.role: Audit/event ledger with as-of capture/replay (ADR 0002).
The projector engine behind compliance findings.
Strangler-fig mappings, ledger, drain.
Declared provider operations + webhook ingress.
SourceRecord landing + chained event ledger.
Mappings-as-data, resolution, survivorship, merge.
Run events from action notifications.
Declared questions, judgment ledger fragments, calibration.
Document versions, addressed atoms, parse runs, assertions.
Plain-data contract that explains a value: steps, typed gaps, PROV-O export.
Serializable rule IR, fact schemas, evaluator seam.
Catalogs/profiles/waivers → immutable bundles; findings projection.
Decisions as versioned resources; TCK-measured.
Decision-document validation (ADR 0027).
The FEEL expression engine (ADR 0027).
Process documents → graph snapshot → token interpreter.
Planning fragments, IR, validators; solver backend.
Governed invocations and durable agent runs (host-instantiated).
The agent-client wire adapter; no second authorization model.
Agent-renderable payloads generated from resources.
Read-only introspection CLI + the iron laws.
Cross-substrate integration battery over its own reference instantiation.
The audit log's hash chain: immutability triggers, the verifier over hot log and archive as one chain, the verified move to the archive.
Masking blocks for sensitive attributes; the generated config's drift gate.
The signature and acknowledgement fragments the host instantiates (ADR 0074).
The version registry the artifact pages read through, and temporal history.
Deterministic PDF documents from Ash data (early; the API may change).

adopted.role: The declarative framework every resource, action and policy is written in.
The data layer; temporal resources, aggregates and codegen live on it.
Forms and LiveView integration for the resources.
Sign-in, tokens, confirmation and password reset.
The sign-in routes and plugs for the authentication package.
The operator-facing admin surface over the resources.
Triggers and scheduled actions on the resources.
Lifecycle state machines on resources that have one.
Soft archival where deletion must not mean loss.
Encrypted attributes (the erasure scopes' payloads).
The money type where amounts are currency-bearing.
One API presentation of the domains.
The other API presentation of the domains.
Tool and prompt-backed action integration for the model plane.
Model calls: key resolution and model selection, owned by the application.
Diagrams generated from the domains.
The dev-only semantic graph and visualization companion.
Tables for the resource lists.
Transactional workflows with compensation (Ash.Reactor).
Durable jobs: triggers, sweeps, drains, workers.
The constraint-solver adapter behind the planning backend.
Dependency usage rules gathered into the agent guidance.
Code generation and project patching.
